top_signals.title: Cuba’s Energy Crisis Turns Into a Goldmine for U.S. Fuel Exporters
top_signals.summary: The Trump administration earlier this year forced a naval blockade on Cuba that brought the island nation to the brink. Now, the U.S. has become Cuba's largest fuel supplier. The blockade has benefited fuel traders. When Washington blocked Cuban ports in January this year, an energy crunch was one of the goals—a shortage of energy commodities, the reasoning went, would prompt regime change, which the Trump administration has openly advocated for.
